misconceptions.description: Writing a reflection that asserts the topic is complicated without naming a specific module principle or its effect on a decision
misconceptions.trigger: learner offers 'it is complicated, there is a lot to consider' as the synthesis
misconceptions.feedback: Name a specific principle from the module and show how it would change a decision you make. 'It is complicated' synthesizes nothing.

misconceptions.description: Believing a module reflection should only recap the readings rather than transfer principles to a new dilemma
misconceptions.trigger: learner equates reflection with summary and avoids applying principles to a fresh situation
misconceptions.feedback: Transfer the principles to a new classroom dilemma. Applied synthesis is stronger evidence of learning than a recap.

misconceptions.description: Submitting AI-generated reflection text, which removes the personal synthesis the studio exists to produce
misconceptions.trigger: learner pastes the prompt into AI and submits the output as their reflection
misconceptions.feedback: Do the synthesis yourself. The studio's value is consolidating the module's principles in your own reasoning; AI output skips that work.

misconceptions.description: Reflecting only on what one now agrees with, with no view that changed and no open tension
misconceptions.trigger: learner lists agreements but names nothing that shifted or remains unresolved
misconceptions.feedback: Surface a point where your view changed or a tension still open. Learning is most visible at those points, not in uniform agreement.
